findings.explanation: variable "kms_key_id" was marked sensitive = true this session. It flows into google_bigtable_instance.pike's cluster.kms_key_name argument, which marks that resource attribute sensitive in Terraform's state/plan. output "instance" exports the whole google_bigtable_instance.pike object without sensitive = true, and Terraform refuses to plan/apply any root module output that transitively contains a sensitive value unless the output itself is marked sensitive. This isn't a static-analysis guess: reproduced empirically in this session with an isolated OpenTofu config (var.s sensitive=true -> resource attribute -> unmarked output) and it fails at 'tofu plan' with 'Error: Output refers to sensitive values'. Deterministic holden rules don't catch this because it requires tracing sensitivity from a variable through a resource attribute into a downstream output block's whole-object reference — a three-hop data-flow analysis, not a single-resource attribute check. Every consumer of this module hits this at plan time, including the module's own example (example/examplea/outputs.tf wraps module.bigtable, which contains .instance, cascading the same error one level up).
findings.remediation: Mark output "instance" as sensitive = true in outputs.tf to make the config valid without reverting the deliberate sensitivity on kms_key_id, then propagate the same change to example/examplea/outputs.tf's output "bigtable" (it wraps module.bigtable, which now contains a sensitive field). Longer-term alternative worth considering separately: output only the specific non-sensitive fields callers actually need (e.g. output "instance_id" { value = google_bigtable_instance.pike.id }) instead of the whole resource object — this avoids redacting harmless fields like the instance name/id for every consumer, and incidentally also stops surfacing the provider's unrelated 'instance_type is deprecated' warning that showed up on the same output during validation.
findings.title: output "instance" transitively exposes the sensitive kms_key_id, breaking terraform plan for every caller

suggested_policies.dsl_extension_note: Needs a new engine-driven policy type (same shape as the existing `engine: iam_escalation` in policies/gcp/iam/escalation-path.yaml, which bypasses the normal `resources:` per-attribute evaluation for a whole-graph analysis). The new engine ('sensitive_output_leak' or similar) must: (1) collect all `variable` blocks with `sensitive = true` plus any `locals`/resource attributes that inherit sensitivity through direct assignment from those variables; (2) walk the HCL reference graph forward from each sensitive source through resource argument assignments to build a set of 'tainted' resource attribute paths (this taint-propagation walk is the part that doesn't exist anywhere in the current evaluator — today's `references`/`requires_companion`/`linked_resource` primitives only check for the *existence* of a graph edge, they don't propagate a value-level property like a sensitivity mark across it); (3) for every root-module `output` block without `sensitive = true`, statically resolve whether its `value` expression syntactically references (as a whole object, or a specific attribute) any tainted resource; (4) fail those outputs. This mirrors Terraform's own native plan-time check but performed at parse time without provider credentials.
suggested_policies.rationale: This is a generic Terraform correctness/data-protection footgun, not GCP- or Bigtable-specific: any sensitive variable that flows into a resource attribute and is then re-exported via an un-marked output block breaks 'terraform plan' for every caller. Terraform itself only catches this at plan time (requires provider credentials and a full graph evaluation); a static holden rule would catch it pre-commit, with no credentials needed, which is exactly the fast-feedback gap holden fills relative to CI-only terraform plan. No existing policy in coverage_by_type for google_bigtable_instance, or any *_iam_binding/*_iam_member type touched by this session's review, covers sensitivity data-flow into outputs — confirmed via grep across the whole policies/ tree for 'sensitive', nothing addresses output-side leakage.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_002
name: Sensitive input values must not reach an unmarked output
principle: data-protection
severity: HIGH
engine: sensitive_output_leak
rationale: |
  A variable declared `sensitive = true` that flows into a resource argument
  marks that resource attribute sensitive in Terraform's state and plan. If a
  root module `output` block references that resource (directly, or as part
  of the whole resource object) without `sensitive = true` on the output
  itself, Terraform refuses to plan or apply — "Output refers to sensitive
  values". This is entirely static and knowable from the configuration alone
  (variable declarations, resource argument assignments, and output value
  expressions), so it does not need a real plan against live credentials to
  catch — but no per-resource attribute-path rule can express it, since the
  failure is a taint that flows through the reference graph: sensitive
  variable -> resource argument -> output value expression.
remediation: |
  Either mark the output sensitive to match the intent of the upstream
  sensitive variable:

    output "instance" {
      value     = google_bigtable_instance.pike
      sensitive = true
    }

  or narrow the output to only the specific non-sensitive fields callers
  need, instead of exporting the whole resource object:

    output "instance_id" {
      value = google_bigtable_instance.pike.id
    }
